name: KubeEdge
what_it_is: KubeEdge is a CNCF-graduated Kubernetes-native edge computing framework that extends containerized application orchestration and device management to edge hosts. It consists of a cloud-side component (CloudCore) and an edge-side component (EdgeCore) that together bridge the Kubernetes control plane with resource-constrained edge nodes.
components: CloudHub — WebSocket server on the cloud side; watches Kubernetes API changes and relays messages to EdgeHub
EdgeController — extended Kubernetes controller managing edge node and pod metadata
DeviceController — extended Kubernetes controller syncing device metadata and status between cloud and edge
EdgeHub — WebSocket/QUIC client on the edge; syncs cloud resource updates to edge and reports status back
Edged — lightweight kubelet-equivalent agent running on edge nodes managing containerized workloads
EventBus — MQTT client (uses mosquitto) enabling pub/sub for edge device communication
ServiceBus — HTTP client enabling cloud components to reach HTTP servers running at the edge
DeviceTwin — stores device status locally at edge and syncs to cloud; provides query interface for apps
MetaManager — message processor between Edged and EdgeHub; persists metadata in SQLite
keadm — CLI tool for bootstrapping cloud and edge nodes (init, join, reset)
protocols: WebSocket (wss://) — primary cloud-edge tunnel on port 10000
QUIC — alternative cloud-edge transport on port 10001
HTTPS — CloudHub HTTPS endpoint on port 10002
MQTT (tcp://) — internal broker on port 1884 and/or external broker on port 1883 for device events
HTTP/REST — ServiceBus bridging cloud-to-edge HTTP servers
Kubernetes API — standard kubectl/CRD-based management surface
measurement: Edge node heartbeat interval (default 15 s) reported to Kubernetes node status
Node status update frequency from Edged (default 10 s)
CloudCore resource limits: CPU 200m max / 100m request, memory 1Gi max / 512Mi request
E2E test polling interval 5 s, timeout 10 min
configuration: CloudCore configured via cloudcore.yaml (ConfigMap): kubeAPIConfig, cloudHub (nodeLimit, TLS certs, WebSocket port, UnixSocket), cloudStream, tunnelPort

EdgeCore configured via edge.yaml: mqtt (server URL, mode, QoS, retain, session-queue-size), edgehub (WebSocket URL, certs, heartbeat), edged (namespace, hostname, interface, docker address, GC thresholds)
MQTT mode: 0 = internal broker only, 1 = internal + external, 2 = external broker only
Modules enabled list in modules.yaml (e.g., eventbus, servicebus, websocket, metaManager, edged, twin, dbTest)
TLS: CA, cert, and key files required at /etc/kubeedge/ca/ and /etc/kubeedge/certs/ for both cloud and edge
CloudHub nodeLimit controls maximum connected edge nodes (default 10)
fault_injection: Edge autonomy mode: edge nodes continue running workloads when cloud-edge network is severed (offline resilience is a first-class design goal, not an add-on)
No dedicated fault-injection framework found in the repository; resilience is tested via e2e suite under tests/e2e/ which exercises node connectivity, pod deployment, and device sync
modes: Cloud mode — run CloudCore on a Kubernetes cluster node (keadm init / cloudcore deployment)
Edge mode — run EdgeCore on a resource-constrained edge host (keadm join)
EdgeSite mode — standalone single-node deployment combining cloud and edge roles (build/edgesite/)
HA mode — multiple CloudCore replicas with shared state (build/cloud/ha/)
Internal MQTT broker only (mode 0), combined internal+external (mode 1), external broker only (mode 2)
constraints: Requires an existing Kubernetes cluster (v1.29–v1.32 for KubeEdge 1.23) — KubeEdge does NOT replace Kubernetes, it extends it
Edge nodes must be able to initiate outbound WebSocket or QUIC connections to CloudHub; inbound connections from cloud to edge are not supported without the tunnel
MetaManager uses SQLite for local metadata persistence — not suitable for high-throughput write workloads at the edge
Edged (EdgeCore) requires a container runtime (Docker or containerd) on the edge host; GPU and device-plugin support is optional and disabled by default
CloudHub nodeLimit (default 10) caps simultaneous edge connections per CloudCore instance
TLS certificates must be pre-provisioned and mounted; keadm handles cert generation during init/join but manual rotation is an operator responsibility
docker_services: kubeedge/cloudcore — CloudCore image (e.g., kubeedge/cloudcore:v1.23.0) deployed as a Kubernetes Deployment with hostNetwork, ports 10000–10004
kubeedge/edgecore — EdgeCore image run as a systemd service (edgecore.service) or container on edge hosts
eclipse-mosquitto (implicit) — MQTT broker referenced by EventBus (tcp://127.0.0.1:1883 external, tcp://127.0.0.1:1884 internal); not bundled, must be deployed separately
No docker-compose file found in the repository — deployment is Kubernetes-manifest-based (build/cloud/) or keadm-driven
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml — the project has no single-command local dev stack; requires a real or kind/minikube Kubernetes cluster
No built-in metrics/observability stack — no Prometheus scrape configs or Grafana dashboards shipped in-repo
No native chaos/fault-injection tooling — resilience relies on network partition tests in e2e suite, not a dedicated framework like Chaos Mesh
No built-in load generator or benchmark harness for edge throughput measurement
